security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI writes debug/trace security configuration fields (SEDBGALW, VSEDBGALW, UEDBGALW, SETRCALW, VSETRCALW, UETRCALW) to the old msdcfg CSR address instead of the new mdtcfg CSR, causing the security policy to silently fail because mdtcfg remains at its reset value (all 0s, i.e., all debug/trace disallowed)
security_spec.summary: CSR rename from msdcfg to mdtcfg splits debug/trace security fields into a new independent CSR; OpenSBI targeting old spec would write to wrong CSR address, leaving mdtcfg at reset-0 and silently disabling all external debug and trace

findings.finding: OpenSBI does not reference msdcfg, mdtcfg, or any debug/trace security fields (SEDBGALW, VSEDBGALW, UEDBGALW, SETRCALW, VSETRCALW, UETRCALW, or any variants). The vulnerability pattern csr_write.*msdcfg|csr_read.*msdcfg|SEDBGALW|SDEDBGALW|SDETRCALW|USEDBGALW|USETRCALW yields zero matches. OpenSBI neither writes to the deprecated msdcfg CSR nor configures debug/trace security policies at all — it delegates this responsibility to platform firmware or leaves it at hardware reset values.
